tasks.title: Create dashboards routing and base structure
tasks.description: Establish core dashboards module with route handlers for Home, Wikis, and Project dashboards. Create base template structure and integrate with shell navigation.
tasks.details:
1. Create `app/routes/dashboards.py` with Flask Blueprint for dashboard routes
2. Implement three route handlers: `/dashboards/home`, `/dashboards/wikis`, and `/dashboards/project/<project_id>`
3. Create `app/templates/dashboards/base.html` with mobile-first responsive grid structure
4. Update `app/shell.py` to add Home Dashboard, Wikis, and Project Dashboard links to sidebar navigation
5. Use existing `app/static/app.css` design tokens for colors, spacing (--gap, --tap), and responsive breakpoints
6. Implement responsive container (max-width: 1280px) for desktop, full-width for mobile
7. Add data attributes for Playwright testing: `data-testid="dashboard-*"`
tasks.testStrategy: Unit test route handlers return 200 status. Integration test sidebar navigation links resolve correctly. Verify base template renders without errors on all routes. Test responsive classes apply correctly at 375px and 1280px viewports using Playwright.

subtasks.title: Create dashboards Blueprint and route structure
subtasks.description: Create the Flask Blueprint module for dashboards with proper routing configuration and three main route handlers
subtasks.details: Create `app/routes/dashboards.py` with a Flask Blueprint named 'dashboards'. Implement three route handlers: `/dashboards/home` (GET), `/dashboards/wikis` (GET), and `/dashboards/project/<project_id>` (GET). Each route should return a basic 200 response for now. Register the Blueprint in `app/__init__.py` with url_prefix='/dashboards'. Ensure routes are accessible and testable.
subtasks.testStrategy: Unit test: verify all three routes return 200 status code. Unit test: verify Blueprint is registered correctly. Integration test: verify routes are accessible via Flask test client with correct URL paths.

subtasks.title: Create base dashboard template structure
subtasks.description: Create responsive base template for dashboards with mobile-first grid layout using existing design tokens
subtasks.details: Create `app/templates/dashboards/base.html` with responsive container structure. Use existing `app/static/app.css` design tokens: --gap for spacing, --tap for touch targets (44px), responsive breakpoints at 860px. Implement max-width: 1280px for desktop, full-width for mobile. Add base grid structure with CSS Grid or Flexbox. Include test data attributes `data-testid="dashboard-home"`, `data-testid="dashboard-wikis"`, `data-testid="dashboard-project"`. Ensure dark theme by default with proper color tokens.
subtasks.testStrategy: Unit test: template renders without errors. Playwright: verify layout at 375px (mobile) and 1280px (desktop) viewports. Verify responsive classes apply correctly. Check for proper spacing using design tokens. No horizontal overflow on mobile.

subtasks.title: Implement route templates for Home, Wikis, and Project dashboards
subtasks.description: Create specific template files for each dashboard with placeholder content and proper inheritance from base template
subtasks.details: Create three template files: `app/templates/dashboards/home.html`, `app/templates/dashboards/wikis.html`, and `app/templates/dashboards/project.html`. Each extends base.html. Add placeholder content blocks for: Home Dashboard (recent sessions, pipelines, backlog summary), Wikis Dashboard (wiki list), Project Dashboard (sprint overview, backlog items, pipelines). Include semantic HTML structure. Add test data attributes for each section (data-testid="sessions-section", etc.).
subtasks.testStrategy: Unit test: all three templates render without errors. Integration test: verify each route serves correct template. Playwright: load each dashboard URL and verify page structure matches expected layout. Check for missing images or resources.

subtasks.title: Update shell navigation to include dashboard links
subtasks.description: Integrate dashboard navigation links into app shell sidebar for Home, Wikis, and Project dashboards
subtasks.details: Update `app/shell.py` to add three new navigation items: 'Home Dashboard', 'Wikis', and 'Project Dashboard'. Add proper links with href attributes pointing to `/dashboards/home`, `/dashboards/wikis`, and context-aware project dashboard URL. Ensure links follow existing navigation styling conventions. Add data attributes for testing (data-testid="nav-dashboard-home", etc.). Update sidebar data structure to include these links. Verify proper icon/styling alignment with existing nav items.
subtasks.testStrategy: Unit test: verify navigation items are generated correctly. Integration test: verify shell renders with new links on all dashboard pages. Playwright: click each navigation link from different pages and verify navigation works. Verify active/highlighted state on current dashboard. Test on mobile (drawer mode below 860px).

subtasks.title: Test responsive design and finalize base structure
subtasks.description: Verify all dashboards render correctly across device sizes and fix any responsive design issues
subtasks.details: Run Playwright tests at both 375px and 1280px viewports for all three dashboards. Verify no horizontal overflow on mobile. Check touch target sizes meet --tap (44px) minimum. Verify grid/spacing uses design tokens correctly. Test navigation drawer behavior on narrow screens (below 860px). Verify all data-testid attributes are present. Check console for errors/warnings. Make any CSS adjustments needed for consistency. Update route handlers to properly render templates with required context variables.
subtasks.testStrategy: Playwright: comprehensive viewport tests at 375px and 1280px for all dashboards. Check touch target sizes. Verify no console errors. Integration test: load all routes and verify correct templates render. Visual check: compare against design spec for spacing, alignment, typography. Test navigation at different breakpoints.

tasks.title: Implement Home Dashboard layout and recent sessions query
tasks.description: Build Home Dashboard template with recent sessions display (5 items), active pipelines (5 items), and recent backlog items (5 items). Implement efficient database queries for all three sections.
tasks.details:
1. Create `app/templates/dashboards/home.html` with three responsive card sections
2. Query recent GENERAL-role sessions (limit 5, ordered by `agent_sessions.updated_at DESC`) from database using SQLite
3. Query active pipelines (status IN [RUNNING, PAUSED], limit 5) from `pipeline_executions` table
4. Query recent backlog items across all projects (limit 5, ordered by `created_at DESC`)
5. Build cards with truncation for long titles (max 50 chars, ellipsis)
6. Add touch-friendly click areas (≥44px) with `.row-actions` pattern for mobile
7. Implement responsive grid: 1 column on mobile (375px), 2-3 columns on desktop (1280px)
8. Use `.table-compact` spacing and app.css color tokens (--bg-secondary, --text-primary, etc.)
tasks.testStrategy: Unit test database queries return correct count and ordering. Mock sessions/pipelines/backlog data and verify rendering. Test card truncation with long titles. Playwright: verify touch targets ≥44px at 375px viewport, no horizontal scroll, all three sections visible. Desktop: verify 2-3 column layout at 1280px. Verify session links navigate correctly.

tasks.title: Implement New Session modal with context selection
tasks.description: Build modal interface for creating new sessions with optional topic and context selection. Integrate with existing session starter and context loaders.
tasks.details:
1. Create modal HTML in Home Dashboard template or separate `_new_session_modal.html` partial
2. Modal form fields: Session role (GENERAL/PLANNING/RESEARCH), optional project context, optional wiki context, optional topic selection
3. Fetch recent GENERAL topics from `app/sessions/topics.py` using `DiscussionTopic.query.filter(DiscussionTopic.archived == False).order_by(DiscussionTopic.updated_at.desc()).limit(5)`
4. Fetch project list from `projects` table for project dropdown
5. Fetch available wiki folders using `app/knowledge/wiki_folders.py` scanner
6. Form submission: POST to `/sessions/new` with context parameters (project_id, wiki_folder, topic_id)
7. Modal styling: use existing modal patterns from app.css (backdrop, card, flex layout)
8. Touch-friendly buttons (≥44px) and form inputs
9. Validate selections (no required fields, allow blank context)
tasks.testStrategy: Unit test topic/project/wiki queries return expected data. Test form submission POST endpoint with various context combinations. Playwright: open modal on mobile (375px) and desktop, verify all fields render, test form submission, verify session is created with correct context. Test empty context (blank session). Test with each context type individually and combined.

tasks.title: Implement Wikis Dashboard with wiki list and search
tasks.description: Build Wikis Dashboard showing available wikis (project + shared), sorted by name, with search functionality and recent docs display.
tasks.details:
1. Create `app/templates/dashboards/wikis.html` template
2. Query wiki folders from `app/knowledge/wiki_folders.py`: use `WikiFolders.scan()` to get all available wikis (project-scoped + shared)
3. Implement wiki search using existing search in `app/wikis/` module (reuse WikiScanner and mistune renderer patterns)
4. Display wiki cards with name, description (if available), doc count, and recent mtime
5. Sort wikis by name alphabetically, with shared wikis at top or bottom (clarify UX preference)
6. Show recent docs per wiki (limit 3) with link to wiki page
7. Responsive layout: 1 column mobile (375px), 2-3 columns desktop (1280px)
8. Search input with real-time filtering (client-side or server-side per performance)
9. Add 'Start Session' action per wiki doc (spawns session with wiki_context set)
10. Use app.css design tokens and `.table-compact` spacing
tasks.testStrategy: Unit test wiki scanner returns expected folders and documents. Test search filtering accuracy (partial match, case-insensitive). Playwright: verify wiki cards render at both viewports, search filters cards in real-time, 'Start Session' action creates session with wiki context. Test with 0, 5, and 20+ wikis. Verify touch targets ≥44px and no horizontal scroll on mobile.

tasks.title: Implement Project Dashboard with sprint and backlog summary
tasks.description: Build per-project dashboard showing current sprint status, backlog breakdown by status, and active pipelines. Add quick action buttons for common workflows.
tasks.details:
1. Create `app/templates/dashboards/project.html` template
2. Accept `project_id` route parameter from `/dashboards/project/<project_id>`
3. Query current sprint from `app/sprints/persistence.py`: `Sprint.query.filter(Sprint.project_id == project_id, Sprint.status == 'active').order_by(Sprint.created_at.desc()).first()`
4. Display sprint card: name, status, task count (from planned_work_items), start/end dates, progress bar
5. Query backlog summary by status: count items per status (Inbox, Ready, In Progress, Done, Blocked) from `backlog_items` table
6. Display status breakdown as cards or horizontal bars (visual clarity)
7. Query active pipelines: `PipelineExecution.query.filter(PipelineExecution.project_id == project_id, PipelineExecution.status.in_([RUNNING, PAUSED])).limit(5)`
8. Display pipeline cards: name, status, execution progress, last updated
9. Quick action buttons (touch ≥44px): 'Start New Sprint', 'Run Pipeline' (dropdown), 'Start Session' (project-scoped)
10. Responsive layout: 1-2 columns mobile, 2-3 columns desktop
11. Mobile sidebar: add project context nav with Project Dashboard link (or inline in main nav when project selected)
tasks.testStrategy: Unit test sprint query with active/inactive sprints, backlog status breakdown query, active pipeline query. Mock project data. Playwright: verify sprint card shows correct data and dates, backlog breakdown totals correct, pipelines list displays with links. Test quick action buttons navigate/open modals correctly. Mobile (375px): verify no horizontal scroll, touch targets ≥44px, single column layout. Desktop (1280px): verify 2-3 column layout. Test with empty sprint, empty backlog, and no active pipelines.

tasks.title: Integrate topic continuation in Home Dashboard
tasks.description: Enhance Home Dashboard New Session modal to display and pre-load recent discussion topics, with rolling summary context preparation.
tasks.details:
1. Extend Home Dashboard template to fetch recent GENERAL topics on page load
2. Query topics: `DiscussionTopic.query.filter(DiscussionTopic.archived == False).order_by(DiscussionTopic.updated_at.desc()).limit(5)`
3. For each topic, fetch rolling summary from `DiscussionTopic.rolling_summary` or reconstruct from topic sessions
4. Add topic selection option to New Session modal: show 'Continue topic: [topic_name]' buttons
5. Update session creation endpoint `/sessions/new` to accept `topic_id` parameter
6. Pass topic context to `app/sessions/starter.py`: set `metadata.topic_id` and pre-load rolling summary into initial prompt context
7. Verify rolling summary is injected correctly by checking session context in starter
8. Add visual indicator (icon, badge) for topics with unread updates or recent activity
tasks.testStrategy: Unit test topic query and rolling summary loading. Test session creation with topic_id parameter and verify context includes rolling summary. Playwright: verify topic list appears in modal, select a topic, verify new session is created with topic context pre-loaded. Test with 0, 5, and 10+ topics. Verify topic rolling summary displays in session starting context (console or test observer).

tasks.title: Implement cross-dashboard deep linking
tasks.description: Add internal navigation links from dashboard cards to related views (wiki card → Wikis Dashboard, sprint card → Project Dashboard, etc.). Support query parameter-based tab/filter selection.
tasks.details:
1. Add href links to all dashboard cards (session, pipeline, backlog, wiki, sprint cards)
2. Home Dashboard session cards → `/sessions/<session_id>` (existing)
3. Home Dashboard pipeline cards → `/dashboards/project/<project_id>?tab=pipelines` (Project Dashboard with pipelines tab selected)
4. Home Dashboard backlog cards → `/dashboards/project/<project_id>?tab=backlog` (Project Dashboard with backlog tab selected)
5. Wikis Dashboard wiki cards → `/dashboards/wikis?wiki=<wiki_id>` or inline wiki viewer (minimal scope for MVP)
6. Wikis Dashboard doc cards → `/projects/<project_id>/wiki/<doc_path>` or session with wiki context
7. Implement query parameter parsing in Project Dashboard: `?tab=sprint|backlog|pipelines` to show/highlight relevant section on load
8. Add breadcrumb navigation or back-link for easy return
9. Test all links across mobile and desktop
tasks.testStrategy: Unit test link generation with various card data. Playwright: navigate via each link type from both mobile and desktop viewports, verify destination page loads and correct tab/section is highlighted. Test query parameter parsing (tab selection). Verify breadcrumbs or back links work correctly. Test deep link directly via URL (copy-paste scenario).

tasks.title: Responsive layout testing and mobile optimization
tasks.description: Comprehensive Playwright testing of all dashboards at 375px and 1280px viewports. Verify touch targets, overflow, truncation, and responsive behavior.
tasks.details:
1. Create/update `tests/test_phase2_ui_verification.py` with dashboard page entries in `_pages` map: home, wikis, project
2. Test Home Dashboard at 375px: verify single-column layout, all 3 sections visible, no horizontal scroll, touch targets ≥44px, card truncation works
3. Test Home Dashboard at 1280px: verify 2-3 column layout, proper spacing, typography scaling
4. Test Wikis Dashboard at 375px and 1280px: search input responsive, wiki cards wrap correctly, doc list scrollable
5. Test Project Dashboard at 375px and 1280px: sprint card responsive, backlog breakdown layout, pipeline list truncation
6. Use helpers: `assert_touch_target_size()`, `assert_no_horizontal_overflow()`, `watch_console()` for errors
7. Test edge cases: long titles (truncate with ellipsis), many items (scrollable list), empty states (no sessions, no wikis, etc.)
8. Verify modal dialogs (New Session) responsive on mobile: full-width modal with scrollable content, buttons below on narrow screens
9. Test responsive font sizing, line heights, spacing across viewports
10. Verify SVG icons/images scale correctly (no distortion)
tasks.testStrategy: Playwright headless tests (do not skip on browser unavailable). Test all dashboard routes at both 375px and 1280px viewports. Assert touch targets, overflow, font sizes, spacing at each viewport. Test edge cases (empty data, long text, many items). Verify responsive classes and media queries work as intended. Use console watching to catch CSS/layout warnings. Run full suite before marking done.

tasks.title: Query performance and caching optimization
tasks.description: Optimize dashboard database queries for performance. Implement caching strategy for frequently accessed data (wiki list, recent sessions, sprint status).
tasks.details:
1. Profile current queries: measure time for session list, pipeline list, backlog summary, wiki scanner
2. Add database indexes on frequently queried columns: `agent_sessions.updated_at`, `backlog_items.created_at`, `pipeline_executions.status`, `sprints.project_id`
3. Optimize N+1 queries: use SQLAlchemy eager loading (joinedload) for related data (e.g., session user, project name)
4. Implement server-side caching for wiki scanner results (mtime-based invalidation, similar to existing wiki implementation)
5. Use Flask cache decorator for dashboard routes (TTL: 30-60 seconds for Home, 60-120 seconds for Wikis and Project)
6. Cache recent topics list (TTL: 120 seconds)
7. Measure page load time before/after optimization using Playwright: `page.evaluate('performance.timing.loadEventEnd - performance.timing.navigationStart')`
8. Set target: Home Dashboard load < 500ms, Wikis Dashboard load < 800ms, Project Dashboard load < 600ms (on typical host)
9. Add cache invalidation on create/update/delete events (e.g., new session → invalidate Home cache)
tasks.testStrategy: Unit test query execution time (mock slow queries, verify optimization improves). Integration test cache invalidation on create/update. Playwright: measure dashboard page load time at both viewports, verify load time meets targets. Test cache hit (reload dashboard, verify quicker load). Test cache miss (create new session, reload Home, verify cache cleared and new data shows). Profile memory usage with many wikis/sessions.

tasks.title: Dashboard polish and finalization
tasks.description: Final refinement: UI polish, animations, edge case handling, documentation, and mark all dashboard features complete.
tasks.details:
1. Review and refine all dashboard templates for consistency (spacing, alignment, typography)
2. Add subtle animations/transitions: card hover effects, modal fade-in, search result fade-in (use CSS transitions, no heavy animations)
3. Handle edge cases: very long titles/names (truncate consistently), empty states (show helpful message), no data (render placeholder cards)
4. Polish empty state UI: add icons, helpful text, suggest next action (e.g., 'No active sprints. Start a new one?' with button link)
5. Verify all links and buttons work: test each action (Start Session, Run Pipeline, Continue Topic, etc.) end-to-end
6. Update documentation: add developer notes to `docs/HIGH_LEVEL_DESIGN.md` or `docs/DASHBOARDS.md` (schema, query patterns, caching strategy)
7. Code cleanup: remove debug logging, verify no console errors in Playwright tests
8. Final visual review at both 375px and 1280px: check alignment, colors (using design tokens), typography scaling
9. Update sidebar navigation labels and help text if needed
10. Verify all responsive classes applied correctly (no hardcoded px values in templates)
tasks.testStrategy: Visual regression test: take screenshots at 375px and 1280px for each dashboard, compare against baseline. Playwright: test all actions end-to-end (create session, select topic, view project dashboard, follow deep links). Test empty state rendering. Verify no console errors or warnings. Manual review: UI polish, animations smoothness, consistency. Run full test suite (including Phase 2 UI verification) and verify all pass.
